content:
Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) slammed Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as a “grifter,” blaming him in part for the U.S. losing its measles elimination status.

Kennedy addressed the Pan American Health Organization’s decision to revoke the country’s elimination status on Tuesday, saying that “routine childhood vaccination” had been interrupted worldwide amid the COVID-19 pandemic, “leaving gaps in protection here and abroad.”

The health secretary stated he’ll “continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles.”

El-Sayed, who has a doctorate in medicine and has worked in public health, called Kennedy’s statement “so disingenuous” in an interview with MS NOW’s Jen Psaki on Tuesday.

“It is COVID-era mis- and disinformation about vaccines generally, a moment in which a grifter used a once-in-a-lifetime pandemic to push his grift to make a huge amount of money for himself and other grifters, that shook a lot of people’s belief in a vaccine that had helped us get to a point where you didn’t have to worry about measles in your kid,” El-Sayed said on Psaki’s show.

The Michigan senator-elect went on to add, “This is one more worry that new parents have to worry about: That their kid will be exposed to a disease that had been previously eradicated because of the mis- and disinformation pushed by the guy who is now HHS secretary.”

Though Kennedy now endorses vaccinating against measles, his messaging on the vaccine has been mixed, including falsely stating the shot causes deaths “every year.”

Kennedy has pushed for alternative “cures” and falsely claimed that getting measles can protect people against cancer. During his tenure as a health official with no medical background, Kennedy has also completely overhauled leadership within the Centers for Disease Control and dismantled childhood vaccination schedules.

El-Sayed also addressed an AI slop image posted by the health secretary very shortly after the U.S. lost its elimination status, showing himself posed as James Bond wielding a large carrot instead of a gun.

“And so for him to now post an image where he’s going to, I don’t know, shoot you with a carrot, it’s just profoundly unserious. And these are serious things. Babies sick with measles. Serious. And that’s what we’re talking about here.”

The senator-elect said he’d like to see “how much money” the health secretary and his associates have made “pushing” alternative treatments.

“Because at the end of the day, when they grift you, there’s always an alternative ... They shake your trust in evidence-based prevention, and then when your trust is shaken, it’s not like they’re just like, well, there’s nothing you can do about it. There’s always something that they’re pushing. So I want to understand where that is,” he said.
